author: Jared B.
text: My Kia Telluride is so comfortable for my family of four plus my kids' friends. It's easy and fun to drive, and it's comfortable as a passenger on road trips. The cup holders and charging ports have been perfect. The Car Play feature has room to grow; Google Maps lags, and music and podcasts don't have the same features as they do from your phone, making it tricky to navigate while driving. The buttons for putting down the second-row seats have been so handy. And I love how the tailgate opens when I stand behind it without having to press any buttons; this is so helpful when my hands are full. The black interior shows every bit of dirt and dust, so if I could change anything about my car, that would be it. The front of the car has been hard to get used to because it sits up high and there are no sensors in the front to tell me when I'm close to something. The seat heaters and ventilation system have been perfect. Overall, I love how quiet the car is and how it blocks road noise. While yes, there are a couple of things I would change, I absolutely love my Telluride and don't regret our decision at all.

author: Quinn E.
text: The 1500 Sierra GMC is probably the best truck on the market in it's class.  This stands out with the engine compartment redesign utilizing the inline 6 diesel with new environmental technology as well as a turbo combining it with the 10 speed transmission. On-the-fly 4WD is awesome. The base options for the SLT was just enough to make the truck enjoyable, I felt the Denali package was over kill; this is still a truck. The AT version is for boys with toys.   The addition of the Rancho shocks makes the ride enjoyable and stiff while pulling a trailer.  It easily pulls a 28 foot trailer and there is little drag and bouncing going over bridges.  Noise cancellation with the carpet wheel base liners as well as the cab foam makes it a quite truck. The tail gate, best on the market. Minor irritation is the interior with regards to the sound system, a joke with little to no bass and only a three bar equalizer and moreover it has terrible interior lighting. The low power LED map light just does not do the job lighting up the cab and I have to use a flash light to see anything. The lighting exterior is great. The biggest concern is the strange noises, like hamsters, when the engine shuts off. This is the turbo actuator decompressing the pressure.  Understandable, but if the vehicle sits and a door is opened, things constantly move under the hood.  If sitting there for five minutes, after decompression, other things just turn on and makes noises. Not sure what it is trying to do. With all of these things happening when the engine is off, brings considerable concern with the longevity of the components. I would like to see some of the parts made in Mexico brought to the US. I see rusting of the bolts already on the under carriage. The interior design is common and far behind FORD and RAM. I think the 2021 models made it more competitive.

I like the Multipro tailgate, it was a great idea... button placement not the best on the back of the tailgate. Also probably should offer a button to put the tailgate back up. My old f150 had a button in the truck bed that allowed me to turn the lights on, the only way to turn the bed lighting on is inside the truck, which makes no sense. The packages make it hard to get exactly what you want on the lot, I would expect automatic windshield wipers in a top trim truck such as the AT4.... I was very displeased to see that it was not included. I am not impressed with the OnStar phone app because they want to charge an excessive fee on a monthly basis for the application. This was free with my past f150 and my current Range Rover Sport. I was not looking for free, but $15 a month for an application that just allows you to lock and unlock your doors as well as remote start your vehicle is completely absurd. This was included with my wife's 2016 Tahoe, I found out (after leasing) it was not included with my wife's 2019 Escalade. We will not be replacing the escalade with another GM product due to this. Not a deal breaker for my pickup as it is a third vehicle. I love the rear seat space, but it is nothing special for a crew cab pickup. The truck does not offer a full sunroof, only over the front of the cab, again not a dealbreaker for an extra vehicle but would have been if I did not have another primary daily driver.

author: Catherine S.
text: This is my 3rd 5-series BMW and I tend to own my cars for about 10 years. This car has some design flaws that I find astonishing when I consider the fact that BMW has some of the best engineers in the world. The storage within the console is also home to the charging port and USB port which I use to connect my phone during my long commute. The phone frequently overheats and shuts down because the compartment gets too hot with the lid closed. In my previous E-60 BMW the center console included a tiny vent for some inbound air conditioned air -- to keep a hardwired phone cool. This may seem insignificant but the fact that I must drive around with the console open is a little silly for a $50K+ car! My 2006 E60 BMW also had navigation but it was able to tell me what city/town I was in. Now with the new format I cannot easily tell where I am. There is a lot to like about the new nav system, but knowing what town I am in seems like it should be on the read-out display. The cup holders are a complete failure! Again, in the E60 the cup holders were actually in front of the A/C vents (brilliant!). If I put a drink in the cup holder on a hot day, the drink was kept cool because of the A/C. Now in the new car the cup holders are in a location that puts them in direct sunlight and away from the A/C. Using the updated cup holders is problematic... in the mornings I usually drink a can of soda on the way to work. The only way to get the can into and out of the cup holder without spilling is to partially crush the can. I have resorted to putting electrical tape over a couple of the holders to easily slide a can into and out of the cup holder without spillage.  Again these are small things,  but as a long time owner and loyal to the brand, I expect more from BMW.

author: Maggie P.
text: Overall, I love my Fiat 500X. I like the unique qualities like the large dashboard that matches the exterior. I wanted something with new technological features, but not anything overly complex. I believe this vehicle is perfect for this. The touch screen is easy to navigate, but offers many features. The Bluetooth is definitely a plus. The vehicle is very roomy and there is a decent amount of storage room (especially in the trunk when you lift up the floor part). The vehicle drives well and accelerates smoothly. MPG is average—nothing impressive. I live in the snow belt and have had no issues driving this vehicle in the snow.

author: Maria P.
text: The Fiat 500 X is a small SUV with AWD.  It's both sporty and practical.  It has plenty of cargo space, can seat five, has comfortable seats and lots of air bags.  It handles well and it's fun to drive.  The three drive modes allow for a choice of all weather traction, best gas mileage, or responsiveness.  Stereo has good sound and pairs well with my iPhone.

author: Frangina C.
text: My Fiat 500 X is great to drive if you want to have fun. It's great for some back roads riding. However, if I could return it I would. The cost of gas was very unexpected. It is my day-to-day car therefore I spend a lot of money on gas. From time to time it has this weird rattling noise in the engine. Aside from that it is a great car, I am just afraid of what could happen and how much money I would have to spend.

author: Henry W.
text: The Fiat 500X with the turbo motor and manual transmission is fun to drive and quick. It is also reasonably economical and practical. Unfortunately, this combination of engine and transmission only comes in the base model, so you sacrifice on technology and luxury features.

author: Laura S.
text: I love how high end my fiat 500x looks. I love how sporty it sounds when I accelerate. I love my sunroof and moon roof.

author: James L.

author: Everett O.
text: The Fiat 500X is a nice SUV, but a little on the small side. I like the power in the engine and it gets good gas mileage. Three downsides for me with this SUV are:1) it can get really loud inside if you're travelling on the expressway with the windows halfway down or even a little bit cracked2) the window button will sometimes do the opposite of what you want (pulling the button up is supposed to raise the window, but sometimes the window will go down)3) due to the size of the SUV, tall people or wide people will not fit too comfortably in the rear. Overall, it has some nice features and for the price, it's a decent buy.

The navigation instructs you on even the most recent changes - where you should be in relation to where you want to go. We've taken it on country roads, potholed roads, on the ferry, and even on the beach - this SUV will not disappoint!
